ai.description: This tortoise reaches 25–30 cm. Its high-domed shell features striking yellow star-shaped patterns on a black background. Deeply grooved, pyramidal scutes distinguish this species.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Indian Star Tortoise is best identified by its high-domed, star-patterned carapace featuring distinct, raised yellow "pyramids" on each scute, unlike the flatter shells of other species.
ai.habitat: The Indian Star Tortoise inhabits semi-arid scrub forests, grasslands, and deciduous thorn forests across the Indian subcontinent, typically at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Indian Star Tortoise is primarily crepuscular, emerging during the cooler dawn and dusk hours to forage for grasses, fallen fruits, and succulent vegetation.
ai.reproductionNotes: Indian Star Tortoises are oviparous, typically nesting during the monsoon season (July–October). They lay 1–3 clutches annually, each containing 1–15 hard-shelled eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Indian Star Tortoise occurs across arid and semi-arid regions of peninsular India, primarily in Gujarat, Rajasthan, and the Deccan Plateau, from sea level to 600m.
